ecus.name: Digital instrument cluster
ecus.function: Renders speed, tachometer / power meter, tell-tales and driver information on a TFT (or drives gauges and a segment display on entry clusters). Graphics MCU with on-chip VRAM on entry / mid clusters (RH850/D1x, TRAVEO T2G cluster), an application SoC with external DRAM on 3D / full-graphic clusters (R-Car D3, i.MX 8, AM62x-Q1, Tegra in early premium units); FPD-Link / LVDS display output, LED backlight driver, CAN / Ethernet, RTC and ambient-light sensing.

pcb.layers: Renesas states that RH850/D1x clusters, which need no external high-speed DRAM, can be designed on lower-cost four-layer PCBs (vendor claim); the Renesas R-Car D3 'Draak' cluster reference board uses a 4-layer through-hole PCB (vendor reference board, not a production cluster). Production cluster layer counts: not published in any source found.
pcb.size: Audi first-generation 12.3-inch LCD cluster (Bosch): main control board 185.0 x 121.3 x 1.70 mm; NVIDIA T30 graphics board 85.12 x 85.01 x 1.24 mm; whole cluster 323 x 190 x 87 mm, 1.6 kg (42how disassembly). Other clusters: not published in any source found.
pcb.technology: Entry / mid clusters: MCU with on-chip VRAM and no external DRAM (Renesas RH850/D1x, 3.5 MB RAM class); premium: SoC + DRAM (Tegra 3 in the Audi unit). HDI / via technology: not published in any source found.
pcb.laminate: not published in any source found
pcb.boards: Audi first-gen LCD cluster: five PCBs - main control board, NVIDIA T30 graphics board, LED driver board for warning lights, two barcode display modules (42how). Visteon 2013 Lincoln MKZ reconfigurable cluster: all circuitry on a single printed wiring board (Visteon statement reported by S&P AutoTechInsight).
pcb.basis: layers: https://www.renesas.com/en/about/press-room/renesas-electronics-introduces-32-bit-automotive-microcontrollers-specialized-instrument-clusters and https://renesas.com/en/products/automotive-products/automotive-system-chips-socs/rtp0rc77995seb0010s-3d-graphics-cluster-r-car-d3-reference-board-draak ; size / boards: https://en.42how.com/2020/07/04/disassembly-of-audis-first-generation-lcd-instrument-cluster/ and https://autotechinsight.spglobal.com/news/19089/visteon-introduces-reconfigurable-instrument-cluster-on-2013-lincoln-mkz ; laminate: no source found

ecus.name: Infotainment head unit / cockpit domain controller
ecus.function: Runs navigation, media, smartphone projection, voice and the centre display(s); in a cockpit domain controller one SoC (Snapdragon SA8155P / SA8295P class) also drives the cluster under a hypervisor. Carries the application SoC + PMICs, LPDDR4X, UFS / eMMC, a vehicle MCU (RH850 class) for CAN / power moding, display and camera SerDes (FPD-Link / GMSL), Ethernet, Wi-Fi / BT, AM/FM / DAB tuner, audio DSP / codec / A2B and often class-D amplifiers.

ecus.name: Telematics control unit (TCU / T-Box)
ecus.function: Cellular connectivity (LTE / 5G network access device, usually a module), GNSS (inside the NAD module or a separate receiver, sometimes with dead reckoning), eCall with a backup battery, charger and boost stage plus an audio codec / amplifier, a vehicle MCU with CAN FD / Ethernet, a secure element / TPM, an accelerometer, and on V2X units a DSRC / C-V2X radio and security element.

boardCostEvidence.claim: IHS teardown (2012): Chrysler UConnect Touch 8.4 head unit BOM $243.94 (top 10 parts ~60%), display unit BOM $129.13; online retail ~$1,700 (list $2,050) for the head unit, ~$1,000 (list $1,270) for the display.
IHS teardown (2012): Honda 39100-SZA-A31 head-end unit total BOM $122.75 (top cost drivers $62.63, 51%).
IHS teardown (2012): Chevrolet Captiva C140 head unit total BOM $103.64 (top cost drivers $68.67, 66%).
IHS teardown (2013): Audi MIB High motorized display unit 8V0857273H6PS total BOM $64.88 (display only, no main processing).
ResearchInChina T-Box report (via ResearchAndMarkets): 5G module prices fell from RMB 1,500 (2019) to RMB 450 (2022); 4G modules cost under RMB 100. These are NAD module prices, not whole-TCU prices.
Retail retrofit price, not a hardware cost: Voyah charged FREE owners RMB 12,999 to upgrade to a Qualcomm 8155 cockpit (includes labour, software, margin).

notes: No public PCB layer count, laminate or placement count was found for any production cockpit SoC board, cluster or TCU; the layer figures above are vendor reference boards (Renesas).

Many cockpit / connectivity chips are sold direct or under NDA (Qualcomm SA8155P / SA8295P / PMM8155AU, Renesas R-Car, Samsung Exynos Auto, MediaTek Dimensity Auto, Autotalks, TI DS90UB98x FPD-Link IV); prices for those are quote only.
The Tesla 4,681-component count is the HW2.5 Autopilot board, not infotainment; it is quoted only to stop it being reused for IVI.
The VW ID.3 ICAS3 processor details come from an owners' community wiki citing FCC filings, not from VW or a teardown house.
BOM figures in boardCostEvidence are 2012-2013 IHS estimates on IHS's own volume assumptions (e.g. 30k/yr for the Desay study); use them as historical benchmarks, not current costs.
